title: Dedicated throughput proving ground and customer onboarding benchmark
creator: Asha Raman
description: Goal: build a deterministic, tenant-aware proving ground for Dedicated capacity that produces a straight‑forward pass/fail artifact for customer acceptance and internal throughput guarantees. Deliverables: 1) orchestration scripts to reproduce throughput runs against a customer-sized tenant mix, 2) a benchmarking methodology doc with signal definitions and gating thresholds, 3) a self-serve customer acceptance checklist and runbook with dashboards and artifacts to attach for signoff. This ticket focuses on the end-to-end experiment harness, metrics contract, and the customer-facing acceptance artifact. Separate work will implement autoscaler tuning and rollout mechanics referenced here.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark harness can reproduce a 30m ramp->sustain->rampdown profile for at least three tenant mixes (small, medium, large) with deterministic inputs.
Pass criteria defined: sustained QPS within +/-10% of expected for 95% of the sustain window across 10 independent runs for each tenant mix.
Tail latency SLOs evaluated and reported: p95, p99 and p999 latencies present with explainable deviations. Any p99 > 500ms must be accompanied by root cause notes.
Automated artifact bundle generated per run: run metadata, load generator config, telemetry links (dashboards), resulting CSV of summary metrics, and a signed run-report for customer onboarding.
Customer-facing acceptance checklist created and validated with Solutions Engineering in at least one pilot onboarding run.
test_plan: Step 1: Provision a dedicated cluster using the dedicated-capacity sandbox script and pin runtime-1.24 + quantization-profile stable-2.
Step 2: Upload three tenant-mix configs to the harness: 'single-tenant-heavy', 'multi-tenant-medium', 'microburst-mix'.
Step 3: Run baseline: 10m warmup -> 30m sustain at target QPS -> 10m cooldown. Repeat 10x per config with fixed seed for request replay.
Step 4: Collect telemetry: request traces, token-per-second, GPU utilization, batch size histogram, KV cache hit rate, error rate, and autoscaler events.
Step 5: Run failure modes: remove 1 GPU mid-run, add noisy background noise, and throttle KV cache for a controlled window to validate graceful degradation and fallback logic.
Step 6: Generate artifact bundle and run-report, then run the acceptance checklist with Solutions Engineering and the pilot customer.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Autoscaler-induced p99 spikes create false negatives for acceptances. Mitigation: run additional experiments with controlled scale-up schedules and include 'exclude window' policy in final report.
Risk: Non-deterministic batch formation across runs. Mitigation: capture batch distribution histograms and add seedable request arrival generator to harness.
Risk: Sensitive customer data exposure when replaying requests. Mitigation: use synthetic or redacted traces; enforce KMS encryption for artifact storage.
